# AI Accountability Standards — Aviation-Grade Accountability Stack for AI Systems

Author: Anthony Cyle Dixon / Contrail Equity Strategies LLC  
Repository: https://github.com/tonydixon417-cmd/ai-accountability-standards  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20883475  
License: CC BY 4.0  
Status: Defensive publication / prior art / open standards framework

## Summary

The AI Accountability Standards repository defines an integrated aviation-grade accountability architecture for large language models and agentic AI systems operating in consequential domains.

The system is designed around a simple premise: AI systems need the same kind of accountability architecture that aviation developed after decades of human-machine failure analysis — flight recorders, warning lights, operating boundaries, recurrent checks, named accountable roles, and independent records that survive the incident.

This is not a single whitepaper. It is a modular accountability stack.

## Core Thesis

AI does not need another chatbot wrapper. It needs a black box, warning lights, a persistent identity layer, and a human accountability structure.

The problem is not that AI dreams. The problem is that it does not know when it is dreaming.

## The Stack

- AI Black Box Standard (AIBB): AI flight recorder; logs outputs, confidence states, session boundaries, and drift events.
- Missing CVR: identifies the missing reasoning/context record in current AI audit systems.
- Loop Detector: detects human-AI accountability loops, automation bias, over-reliance, and mode confusion.
- Persistent Identity Layer (PIL): preserves user context, values, decisions, and identity across sessions and platforms.
- ZeroTX Architecture: data-sovereignty architecture for local, federated, or enterprise-controlled AI processing.
- Ethics Floor / Covenant Warning System: establishes ethical and operational terrain boundaries.
- AI Preflight Briefing Standard: requires session-start disclosure of capability, confidence, boundaries, and role.
- AI Type Rating Framework: scales operator certification to the consequence level of the AI system.
- Chief AI Accountability Officer (CAAO): defines a named accountable human role for enterprise AI deployment.
- Distributed Oversight Model: prevents the accountability officer or deploying organization from becoming a single point of failure.
- Early Warning Channel: lets human operators log “something feels wrong” before a formal failure threshold is crossed.
- ZeroTX Deployment Tiers: defines Pure, Federated, and Enterprise deployment models.
- Check-Ride Protocol: recurrent evaluation system that detects whether human reviewers remain actively engaged or are rubber-stamping AI output.

## Recommended Reading Path

1. AI Black Box Standard (AIBB)
2. Loop Detector
3. Persistent Identity Layer (PIL)
4. ZeroTX Architecture
5. Missing CVR
6. Distributed Oversight Model
7. Early Warning Channel
8. ZeroTX Deployment Tiers
9. Check-Ride Protocol

## Domains

Relevant to healthcare AI, legal AI, financial AI, insurance AI, government AI, enterprise AI governance, AI auditability, model risk management, AI compliance, EU AI Act readiness, human-AI oversight, responsible AI, AI incident response, and agentic AI safety.

## Companion Book

The Becoming is the human-factors and narrative companion to this technical standards stack. The book explains why the accountability architecture is necessary; this repository documents the architecture itself.
